doc.title: Phil Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 27, 2023

title: Road years: Dorsey, Belletto, and the NORAD band
summary: He recalls staying on the road through Dorsey, Al Belletto, the NORAD band and Woody Herman, learning mic technique, arranging and soloing.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: When I think of you young men on the bus I guess there are some stories about Woody Herman and the bus trips.
What did you do on the bus to pass the time? This was well before people could stare at their phones all day or well before having a disc player. How did you pass the time? © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-

Very, very comfortably in a way. I mean I’m — 18, 19, 20 I went out with the Dorseys at 20 and basically I stayed on the road until I left Woody’s band in ’67? It can’t be that long. I must be exaggerating. But still we’re talking the Dorsey band, Al Belletto’s group for half a year going into the army, the navy NORAD band — North American Air Defense Command — and that’s where I learned all my technique I know about how to microphone etcetera, etcetera. I learned how to get my own sound. I recorded all these records for NORAD for two years out in Hollywood. We recorded two months of the year for two years. And I got to work on my arranging and composition and having it played on a daily basis. I learned to solo over, and write my own charts and things like that. They were not world leaders but they sure did help me learn my craft.
